total_warnings.title: Total Warnings

JobCompletionIssue.description:
Why a COMPLETED job delivered no document.

Read for what a run did; the verdict only says whether anything was lost. A run whose
source handed back nothing finishes `processing_status: SUCCESS` with an empty
destination, and without this there is no statement anywhere that it moved nothing
(Pylon 2287, PLU-622). A run that discovered documents and delivered none of them
without failing any is FAILED, and carries this for the same reason: nothing else on the
row explains it. A run whose documents failed carries none of these; `/failed-files`
explains it.

So the verdict cannot be used to find these runs, and a caller that wants to know
whether a job delivered anything branches on this field.

Its own type on its own nullable field, deliberately NOT a `JobProcessingStatus`
member: that enum is on the public wire and a closed generated-SDK enum breaks a
whole `list_jobs` page on one unrecognised value (DTPL-696, `REJECTED`).

Null is "no issue detected", never "checked and fine" -- a caller must not read the
absence of a value as a guarantee, and a job FAILED for some other reason (a failed
document, a preflight rejection) carries none of these. New members may be added; treat
an unrecognised one as "an issue was detected, of a kind this client does not know".
JobCompletionIssue.title: JobCompletionIssue

completion_issue.description: Why a job completed without delivering a document. Not a restatement of the verdict: a run whose source handed back nothing lost nothing and reports `processing_status: SUCCESS`, so this is the only account of its empty destination. `NO_DOCUMENTS_DISCOVERED` -- the job completed without a single document being discovered at its source, so nothing was processed and nothing delivered. `NO_DOCUMENTS_SUCCEEDED` -- documents were discovered and none of them succeeded, with none recorded as failed either, so `/jobs/{job_id}/failed-files` has nothing to show. Null means no issue was detected, never that the run was checked and found fine; a job FAILED for any other reason (a failed document, a preflight rejection) carries none of these. Set only once the settle window has passed, the same window `processing_status` holds IN_PROGRESS for. New values may be added; treat an unrecognised one as an issue of a kind this client does not know.

processing_status.description: Authoritative processing outcome. For a just-completed job this stays IN_PROGRESS for a short settle window (until per-document counts finalize) before resolving to SUCCESS, COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS or FAILED. COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS means every document finished but some carried a step's notice; see `warning_nodes`. Poll until it leaves SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS; do not infer success from JobInformation.status alone.

progress.description: Why this job is not finished yet: whether it has started, when its steps last moved, and what else is running in this workspace. Null means only that this server did not compute a reading, never that the job is fine. Advisory -- it is a read of per-node counters, not the clock that terminates a job.

queued_behind_job_ids_snapshot.description: Job ids that held this workspace's concurrency slots at the instant this run was queued. Taken once and never refreshed, so the jobs named here may have finished long ago. It is not the set of jobs this run is waiting on, and it errs in both directions: runs queued ahead of this one but not yet started sit on the FIFO queue rather than in a slot, so they are absent; and the snapshot is taken at queue time whether or not the jobs it names are what kept this run waiting, since a held slot is not by itself the workspace being full at its `tenant_max_concurrent_jobs` limit. Show it as what held a slot at that moment, never as the cause of a delay or as a complete list of blockers. Null means no snapshot exists -- the run did not go through the queue, or the read failed -- which is not the same as `[]`, meaning the snapshot was taken and nothing held a slot. For what is running now, read `progress.other_active_jobs`, which is a live read.
queued_behind_job_ids_snapshot.title: Queued Behind Job Ids Snapshot

warning_nodes.description: Which steps reported notices, with how much work they reported undone (`num_notices`, counted as in `total_warnings`) and on how many documents (`num_docs`). Empty when none did. GET /jobs/{job_id}/file-status lists the notices per file.
warning_nodes.title: Warning Nodes

next_offset.description: Next page start, or null at the end of the available artifact.
next_offset.title: Next Offset

total.description: Failure entries available in this report, before pagination. Counts file/node pairs, not unique documents. Older data planes may have capped the artifact; this count cannot recover or detect those omitted entries. Reports refresh periodically and at finalization. Present when paging.
total.title: Total

JobFileStatuses.description: Every file's processing status for one job.

generated_at.description: When the data plane produced the underlying report; it trails live execution.
generated_at.title: Generated At

index_finished.description: True once no source connector is still listing files, so no further files will arrive from one. A source whose node failed counts as finished. A listing that failed while its node is still live does not: it is retried, so a failed job can end with this false. Read the job's own status alongside it. Not a promise that this list is final: a workflow step can still introduce files afterwards, which discovered_by_node_id (on each file) tells apart from what a source listed. Null when the job cannot say, which today means a resident job, or when the data plane does not report it.
index_finished.title: Index Finished

truncated.description: True when the data plane hit its per-job file cap, so this is a subset of the job's files rather than all of them. The cap selects files in id order, so the subset is arbitrary -- treat an absent file as unknown, not as missing.
truncated.title: Truncated

JobFileStatuses.title: JobFileStatuses

completion_issue.description: Why a job completed without delivering a document. Nothing else on the row says it: `failed_file_count` is 0, `reason` is null and `GET /jobs/{job_id}/failed-files` is empty. A job whose source handed back nothing lost nothing and reports `processing_status: SUCCESS`, so this is the only account of its empty destination; a job that discovered documents and delivered none is FAILED with nothing else to explain it. `NO_DOCUMENTS_DISCOVERED` -- the job completed without a single document being discovered at its source. `NO_DOCUMENTS_SUCCEEDED` -- documents were discovered and none succeeded, with none recorded as failed either. Null means no issue was detected, never that the run was checked and found fine; a job FAILED for any other reason carries none of these. Same value `GET /jobs/{job_id}/details` returns. New values may be added; treat an unrecognised one as an issue of a kind this client does not know.

failed_file_count.description: Documents that failed so far. Read it against `processing_status`, which says whether the job has reached a verdict: on a job that has not finished, 0 means none recorded yet, not that every input produced output.
failed_file_count.title: Failed File Count

processing_status.description: Document-level outcome, as opposed to `status`, which is only a lifecycle state. FAILED here with status COMPLETED means the job ran to completion but at least one document did not survive it. Read `failed_file_count` for how many, and GET /jobs/{id}/failed-files for why. COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS means no document failed but at least one carried a notice from a step, such as enrichment that did not run after its retries were exhausted; GET /jobs/{id}/file-status?has_warnings=true lists those documents.

reason.description: Sanitized failure reason for a FAILED job; None otherwise.
reason.title: Reason

status.description: Job lifecycle state. COMPLETED means the job finished executing; it does not indicate whether documents succeeded. For the processing outcome, read processing_status on this response where it is present, or from GET /jobs/{id}/details. Job-creation responses (POST /jobs/ and POST /workflows/{id}/run) omit it, because nothing has been processed yet.

failure_category.description: Why this node failed its preflight check. Set only on a `REJECTED` job, and only on the node that failed -- a node that passed is null. Route on this rather than `failure_reason`, and treat an unrecognised value as `UNKNOWN`.

failure_reason.description: Human-readable detail, forwarded from the provider. Free-form and unstable: it changes with third-party error text, so show it to a person and never parse it.
failure_reason.title: Failure Reason

last_change_at.description: When this step last reported new counts. Null when it has not reported at all. Source steps never report, so they are listed here with this field null rather than being left out. Stager steps are not DAG nodes and are never listed. It means this step's counters changed, not that a document finished: a document moving from ready to in progress moves this too.
last_change_at.title: Last Change At

node_id.description: Id of this step in the workflow DAG. This is the key `progress.slowest_node_id` names -- join on it rather than on `node_name`, which is mutable. A saved workflow's node id is a UUID; a custom DAG's is whatever its author called it. Null on the standalone job shape, whose spec does not guarantee a node id.
node_id.title: Node Id

node_phase.description: The node's Kubernetes workload state, independent of document counts. Null means no lifecycle snapshot has ever been received for this node -- an older data plane, or the producer turned off -- and never that the node is idle. A job that has ended drops the phases that promise its workload is still coming up (`PENDING_CREATE`, `SCHEDULING`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`), but a job that ended badly keeps a blocked phase (`UNSCHEDULABLE`, `UNSTARTABLE`, `CRASH_LOOPING`): it says how the run ended. Treat an unrecognised value as `UNKNOWN`.

node_phase_observed_at.description: When the data plane observed the phase. Trails live cluster state.
node_phase_observed_at.title: Node Phase Observed At

JobNodePhase.description:
Runtime state of a DAG node's Kubernetes workload. NOT document counts.

An unrecognised value reads as UNKNOWN.
JobNodePhase.title: JobNodePhase

JobNoticeNode.description: One workflow node's share of the plugin notices a job's files carried.

node_id.description: Id of the workflow node that reported them. Join it against the job's DAG.
node_id.title: Node Id

num_docs.description: How many files carried at least one of them.
num_docs.title: Num Docs

num_notices.description: How much work the node reported undone (see `total_warnings`).
num_notices.title: Num Notices

Why this job is not finished yet, as of `as_of`. Advisory: a heuristic read of
per-node counters, not a contract, and not the clock that terminates a job.

as_of.description: When this progress read was computed. Every age in this object is measured from here, not from when you received the response.
as_of.title: As Of

last_node_change_at.description: The most recent time any step reported new counts. Null when no step has reported at all -- read `nodes_observed` to tell that case apart. It means the counters changed, not that a document finished: a document moving from ready to in progress moves this too.
last_node_change_at.title: Last Node Change At

message.description: The measurement stated for a person. One or more sentences -- the step the job is sitting in, a pending stop, cancelling as an option and the other jobs running in this workspace are each appended when they apply. Free-form and unstable: the wording changes between releases, so display it and never parse it.
message.title: Message

nodes_observed.description: How many steps have reported counts. 0 means none has yet. Source and stager steps never report, so a job wedged fetching its source reports 0 here instead of naming the step it is stuck in.
nodes_observed.title: Nodes Observed

other_active_jobs.description: Other `SCHEDULED` or `IN_PROGRESS` jobs in this workspace, oldest first. The list is capped, so read `other_active_jobs_total` for how many there really are. These jobs share the workspace; none of them is asserted to be blocking this one. Empty whenever `state` is `not_applicable`, where the workspace is not measured at all.
other_active_jobs.title: Other Active Jobs

other_active_jobs_total.description: Uncapped number of other non-terminal jobs in this workspace. It can exceed the length of `other_active_jobs`; quote this number, not the list length. Reads 0 whenever `state` is `not_applicable`, which means not measured rather than none running -- ask `GET /jobs/` if you need the workspace count beside a finished job.
other_active_jobs_total.title: Other Active Jobs Total

outstanding_docs.description: Documents still ready or in progress at `slowest_node_id`, null whenever that is null. This is the number `message` states, carried as an integer so it never has to be parsed back out of the prose.
outstanding_docs.title: Outstanding Docs

seconds_since_node_change.description: Seconds between `last_node_change_at` and `as_of`. Null when no step has reported, and null when that timestamp is in the future -- these are pod clocks, so a negative age is reported as unmeasurable rather than as 0. A step grinding one large document holds its counts constant while perfectly healthy, so a large value is a measurement, not a verdict that the job is broken.
seconds_since_node_change.title: Seconds Since Node Change

seconds_without_report.description: How long this job has gone with no step reporting any work, in seconds. Measured from submission while it is waiting to start, and from when it started running once it is running. Null once `nodes_observed` is above 0 -- read `seconds_since_node_change` from that point on.
seconds_without_report.title: Seconds Without Report

slowest_node_id.description: The step with work still outstanding whose counts are oldest -- where the job currently sits. Null when no step has outstanding work. This says where the job is, not that this step is at fault.
slowest_node_id.title: Slowest Node Id

slowest_node_name.description: Display name of `slowest_node_id`, null whenever that is null. Names are mutable -- key on `slowest_node_id`, which every entry in `node_stats` carries as its own `node_id`.
slowest_node_name.title: Slowest Node Name

state.description: What this job is doing right now, in one value. Route on this rather than on `message`, and treat an unrecognised value as `unknown`. It is a read of per-node counters, so it is advisory: it is not the clock that terminates a job, and `unknown` never means the job is fine.

stop_requested_at.description: When a stop was requested for this job, null if none was. A job with this set is already cancelling, so do not cancel it again.
stop_requested_at.title: Stop Requested At

get.description:
The workspace the credential acts in and the account that workspace belongs to. Use `account_id` with the account-scoped routes, such as `/api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/consumed`.

Authenticate with an API key, or a bearer token of a member who can read the workspace's metadata. With a bearer token the workspace is the token's own or the one named in `X-Workspace-Id`. Nothing about any other workspace or account is returned.

A workspace that belongs to no account answers 403, and a failure to look the account up answers 503.

Call this endpoint at most 15 times per minute for each authenticated identity.
get.summary: Account and workspace of this credential

get.description:
Units an account consumed over a window: the number its licence allowance is enforced against, summed over every workspace of the account.

Authenticate with an API key of any workspace in the account, or a bearer token of a member with permission to read the account's billing information. Any other account answers 403.

Counted in whole UTC days. Days before the counter began (`counted_from`) count as zero. A window that ends after today answers 503 rather than a smaller number, and so does any failure to read the count: a 200 is never a stand-in for a count that could not be read.

`breakdown=day` adds `days`, the quantity for every UTC day in the window (at most 366 days), for charting; weeks and months roll up from it.

`split=strategy` adds `strategies`: the pages by processing strategy (`fast`, `hi_res`, `vlm`), with `other` for every other kind of page and `unattributed` for pages counted before the split began (`strategies_counted_from`) or asserted as an opening balance. The five always sum to the quantity they split. The split is informational: the licence counts every page as one, whatever its strategy.

Call this endpoint at most 15 times per minute for each authenticated identity.

parameters.description: Unit to count. Today only `pages`.
parameters.name: unit

parameters.description: Start of the window, RFC 3339. Counted in whole UTC days: the day containing `start` counts in full.
parameters.name: start

schema.description: Start of the window, RFC 3339. Counted in whole UTC days: the day containing `start` counts in full.
schema.title: Start

parameters.description: End of the window, RFC 3339. Counted in whole UTC days: the day containing `end` counts in full, unless `end` is exactly midnight UTC, which ends the window with the previous day.
parameters.name: end

schema.description: End of the window, RFC 3339. Counted in whole UTC days: the day containing `end` counts in full, unless `end` is exactly midnight UTC, which ends the window with the previous day.
schema.title: End

parameters.description: `day` adds `days`: the quantity for every UTC day in the window, at most 366 days.
parameters.name: breakdown

schema.description: `day` adds `days`: the quantity for every UTC day in the window, at most 366 days.
schema.title: Breakdown

parameters.description: `strategy` adds `strategies` to the total, and to each of `days`: pages by processing strategy (`fast`, `hi_res`, `vlm`, `other`, `unattributed`), summing to the quantity they split. Informational: every page counts as one against the licence.
parameters.name: split

schema.description: `strategy` adds `strategies` to the total, and to each of `days`: pages by processing strategy (`fast`, `hi_res`, `vlm`, `other`, `unattributed`), summing to the quantity they split. Informational: every page counts as one against the licence.
schema.title: Split

get.description: Retrieve failed files for a specific job. Omit paging parameters for the legacy sample response. Supply limit (1-1000) or offset to page through the complete report on upgraded data planes, with pagination metadata; offset alone uses a page size of 500. Pages follow the stored report order. For a stable traversal, wait for the job and its final failure report to finish; reports can change while a job runs. Older data planes may have truncated the stored report, so pagination cannot recover entries missing from that artifact. Call this endpoint at most 60 times per minute for each job and authenticated identity.

Retrieve the processing status of every file in a job: one entry per file, carrying its status for the whole job and the workflow step it currently sits at, plus its `notices`; `has_warnings` keeps only the files that carry one. Complements `/jobs/{job_id}/details`, which reports the same work as per-node counts, and `/jobs/{job_id}/failed-files`, which covers failures only. Call this endpoint at most 12 times per minute for each job and API key or JWT identity. For source-listed files, filter by `discovered_by_node_id`; that subset is complete when `index_finished` is true and `truncated` is false. Read the job status alongside this response because a failed source also counts as finished.

parameters.description: true returns only files that carry a notice (non-empty `notices`), false only files that carry none. Omit for every file.

schema.description: true returns only files that carry a notice (non-empty `notices`), false only files that carry none. Omit for every file.
